sections.h2: Which Edison offices send and collect the tax bill?
sections.html:
Edison's Tax Collector bills and collects more than 30,000 tax accounts and a similar number of sewer accounts. The office is on the second floor of the municipal building at 100 Municipal Blvd., open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and reachable at 732-248-7228 or TaxCollector@EdisonNJ.gov. The Tax Assessor, a separate office, keeps data on more than 28,000 properties and takes the state deduction applications.

Edison sits in Middlesex County, so assessment appeals go to the Middlesex County Board of Taxation, and the assessor coordinates the township tax map with that board. The collector cannot change a value, and the assessor cannot take a payment.

  • Collector: bills, receipts, payoff figures and sewer accounts.
  • Assessor: ownership records, property data, mailing address changes and deductions.
  • County board: formal appeals of value.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Edison for a home seller?
sections.html:
Edison is a 30-square-mile township of roughly 109,000 people in the Raritan Valley, and it wraps around the borough of Metuchen. Thomas Edison's Menlo Park laboratory, where the light bulb was perfected, gave the township its name in 1954, replacing the old name of Raritan Township. About 27 miles separate it from both Midtown Manhattan and Trenton.

The economy rests on Raritan Center, a 2,300-acre business park that includes the New Jersey Convention and Exposition Center, with regional distribution hubs for national carriers. Older manufacturing left the area in the 2000s, and the Ford plant that once stood in Edison was demolished by 2008 and replaced with retail. Neighborhood names on a listing include Menlo Park, Oak Tree, Clara Barton, Stelton, Raritan Manor and Lincoln Park. Route 1, Route 27, Route 440 and Interstate 287 cross Edison, and the New Jersey Turnpike has its Exit 10 here. Two high schools, Edison High in the south and J.P. Stevens in the north, split the public school district of 19 schools.

The township counts about 307 miles of roadway, and it maintains 257 of them, with Middlesex County, the state and the Turnpike Authority covering the rest. Winters are cool to cold with snow every year, and summers are hot and humid, so roof, gutter and drainage condition tend to come up in inspections.

  • Census estimate for July 2025: 109,077 people, against 107,400 at the 2020 base.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 through 2024: $496,900.
  • Owners live in 60.6 percent of homes, and median gross rent is $1,974.
  • Median household income: $125,145, with 47.7 percent of residents foreign-born.

sections.h2: When is Edison property tax due?
sections.html:
Edison taxes are due on the first of February, May, August and November, and the grace period is 10 days, or until Monday if the tenth is a weekend. Bills go out once a year, usually in June or July, with four stubs: August and November of the current year and February and May of the next. If no bill has arrived by August 1, call the collector, because a missing bill still leaves you responsible.

Edison installment schedule, per the Tax Collector's billing notice
InstallmentDue date
Third quarterAugust 1
Fourth quarterNovember 1
First quarterFebruary 1
Second quarterMay 1

Interest on a late payment is up to 8 percent a year on the first $1,500 and 18 percent beyond that, running from the original due date once the grace period has passed. A penalty of up to 6 percent can apply to a total delinquency above $10,000 left unpaid at year end. Any municipal charge still unpaid on November 11 is subject to the tax sale.

sections.h2: How do you pay in Edison, and what happens with a mortgage escrow?
sections.html:
Take cash, a check or a money order to the second floor of the municipal building, use the curbside drop box, mail a check, or pay online through the township's payment page. Mailed payments count on the day they arrive, not the day of the postmark, and drop box payments are posted the next business day. Make checks payable to Edison Tax Collector, never postdate them, and expect a $20 charge on a returned check.

  • With an escrow account, the lender gets the original bill and you get an advice copy.
  • Paid off your mortgage? You can use the advice copy to make the next payment and tell the collector who now pays.
  • For a receipt by mail, send the entire bill and a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

sections.h2: How is an Edison sewer bill different from the tax bill?
sections.html:
Edison sewer charges are billed once a year, based on the prior year's water use, and paid in two halves. The first half is due on the date printed on stub one, usually between April and June, and the second is due October 1. The property owner owes the bill, and a mortgage lender does not pay it unless you arrange that yourself.

Residential customers get a 15 percent outside water discount that is already taken off the bill. Owners 65 or older who prove their age by March 1 get a rate freeze on their primary residence, and a Senior Center card can serve as proof. When a house sells, the sewer bill goes to the new owner or the title company, so confirm both accounts are current before closing.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an Edison assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition of appeal with the Middlesex County Board of Taxation by April 1, or by May 1 if Edison has just completed a revaluation. The petition has to be received by the deadline, and you must serve the Edison assessor and municipal clerk. Only value can be appealed. Prove what the house was worth on October 1 of the prior year with no more than five comparable sales.

The filing fee runs from $5 to $150 depending on assessed value, and the board's judgment holds for the year and the next two unless something changes the assessment. Call the Middlesex board for its hearing schedule, and the Edison assessor for questions on the property record card. The assessor's office also processes the $250 deductions for qualified veterans, seniors and disabled owners, plus the full exemption for a 100 percent disabled veteran.

sections.h2: What if you owe Edison property tax and want to sell?
sections.html:
You can sell with tax still owing. The closing agent pays the amount from the proceeds after getting a payoff figure from the collector, dated for the closing day. Ask for the interest per day, since a few extra days can change the number.

The state's homeowner guide warns that taxes still open after the November installment can lead to a lien, that a lien must be redeemed before the house is sold, and that a lien holder can start foreclosure after two years. In Edison, a balance left on November 11 is eligible for the tax sale. Settling it before listing keeps the sale simpler.

faqs.q: Where is the Edison Tax Collector?
faqs.a: On the second floor of the municipal building at 100 Municipal Blvd., Edison, NJ 08817, open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone is 732-248-7228.

faqs.q: How long is the Edison tax grace period?
faqs.a: Ten days after the due date printed on the stub. When the tenth day lands on a weekend, it extends to Monday.

faqs.q: When is the second Edison sewer payment due?
faqs.a: October 1. The first half is due on the date shown on stub one, usually between April and June.

faqs.q: Does a postmark count for an Edison payment?
faqs.a: No. The office must receive the payment by the end of the grace period, and drop box payments are posted the next business day.

faqs.q: Which county board hears Edison appeals?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Board of Taxation, by April 1, or May 1 after a township-wide revaluation.
